extracted.intended_audience: F99/K00 grant applicants, mentors, and grant reviewers in aging, dementia, and mixed-methods research
extracted.subtask_description: Research and training plan for an F99/K00 career development grant proposing mixed-methods longitudinal analyses and intervention co-design to examine physical/social environments, social isolation, and cognitive health among older adults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Latent growth curve modeling (LGCM) & model fit criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Latent growth curve modeling (LGCM) will be employed to model the longitudinal relationships between physical environments, social environments, social isolation, and cognitive health. LGCM allows nested models at hierarchical levels and is a special case of structural equation modeling (SEM) well suited for modeling mediation (H3, H6) and testing moderating effects of ICT use (H7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate model fit using RMSEA, CFI, and TLI. RMSEA < 0.05, CFI and TLI > 0.90 are considered acceptable; CFI and TLI > 0.95 indicate good model fit. Run LGCM models with Mplus 8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multicollinearity detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze and detect any potential multicollinearity issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct diagnostics prior to model estimation to ensure predictors are not collinear; adjust modeling strategy if multicollinearity is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Full Information Maximum Likelihood (FIML) for missing data
rubrics_metrics.description: Full Information Maximum Likelihood (FIML) estimation will be used to handle missing data in models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIML is a single-step maximum likelihood approach widely used in SEM and appropriate for handling missing data under MAR assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply sampling weights for representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Sampling weight will be applied to the models to match the representativeness of the racial/ethnic groups as designed in the sampling strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate sampling weights in model estimation so results reflect the intended population composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative recruitment: purposeful sampling with maximum variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus group participants will be recruited purposefully among current I-CONECT participants using a strategy of maximum variation: individuals with diverse living environment conditions, selected from both study sites (OHSU & UM). Two focus groups will be held at each site: one with intervention-group participants, the other with control-group participants. It is targeted for each focus group to have 8 participants (total N=32). To avoid contamination, only participants who have completed I-CONECT will be invited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use purposeful selection to capture heterogeneity in living environments and site/treatment status; plan recruitment and timing to avoid intervention contamination; align qualitative timeline with F99–K00 phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview guide development and expert consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: The interview guide will be developed informed by concepts in ETA and in consultation with experts with qualitative/mixed-methods research specialties and with the best knowledge of I-CONECT participants. The PD/PI will facilitate the focus groups at both sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft guides informed by theory (ETA) and expert input; involve those with direct knowledge of the population to ensure relevance and feasibility; have PI facilitate to maintain consistency across sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative data collection procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversations in focus group sessions will be audio-recorded and then transcribed verbatim for analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure high-quality audio recording, verbatim transcription, and secure data storage; plan procedures for participant consent regarding recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative data analysis: inductive coding, multiple coders, and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Transcripts will be analyzed using an inductive content analysis method by at least two trained independent coders collaborating with Nvivo 12. The coding team will meet regularly to discuss the coding framework, procedure, and to reconcile differing opinions and interpretations. Cohen’s kappa coefficient will be employed as the indicator for inter-rater reliability. Themes will be reorganized according to personal and living environmental characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use at least two independent coders, qualitative analysis software (Nvivo 12), regular reconciliation meetings, and quantitative inter-rater reliability (Cohen’s kappa) to document coding consistency; organize themes to reflect contextual participant characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed-methods integration: concurrent explanatory design and use of qualitative data
rubrics_metrics.description: The qualitative and quantitative inquiries will occur concurrently. The main purpose of adopting mixed-methods is using qualitative data to explain why there might be effects of physical and social environments on social isolation. Qualitative focus groups expand discussions on quantitative findings and elicit participants’ insights on designing a sustainable environmental-focused technology program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct concurrent data collection and integrate qualitative explanations into interpretation of quantitative results; use combined findings to inform intervention development and pilot testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: I-CONECT randomized trial design
rubrics_metrics.description: I-CONECT is conducted at OHSU and UM. One hundred sixty socially isolated adults aged 75+ will be recruited at each site and randomized into either the video-chat intervention group or the control group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement randomized allocation across sites with clear enrollment targets; register trial (ClinicalTrials.gov ID provided) and report accrual progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: I-CONECT inclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion criteria: aged 75 or older, consent to MRI if eligible, socially isolated, adequate vision and hearing, understand English, and normal cognition or MCI (based on consensus diagnosis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these eligibility criteria consistently during screening to define the trial population and ensure safety for MRI procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention dosing and contact schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Intervention group participants receive computers and internet service and are scheduled for video chat with study staff for 30 minutes/day, 4 times/week for 6 months (high dose), and 2 times/week for an additional 6 months (maintenance dose). Study staff briefly check in by phone (~10 minutes) with both intervention and control participants once per week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and adhere to intensity (high vs maintenance) schedules; provide necessary technology to ensure access; standardize phone check-ins across groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment schedule and recording for language analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: In-home neuropsychological assessments will be administered at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months. All participants would have MRI scans at baseline and 6 months if MRI were safe. All video chat and in-home assessment sessions are recorded for language analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule assessments at pre-specified time points, obtain MRI safety consent, and systematically record sessions for subsequent language/speech analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medication adherence measurement via electronic pillboxes (digital biomarker)
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical adherence measured with electronic pillboxes. Compared to self-reported adherence, the digital biomarker collected with electronic pillboxes can eliminate social desirability bias and record the exact time when participants opened the pillboxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use objective electronic monitoring devices to capture adherence timing and reduce bias inherent in self-report measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome measurement standards (cognitive, MRI, speech, social isolation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary intervention outcomes are executive and memory functioning assessed with the National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center Uniform Data Set neuropsychological battery (UDS V3), cross-validated by NIH Toolbox. Region-specific structural and functional pre-post changes in the brain are evaluated with MRI. Speech and language characteristics are captured during each video chat and in-home assessments. Social isolation is defined as i) Score ≤12 on the 6-item Lubben Social Network Scale (LSNS-6); or ii) Engages in conversations lasting 30 minutes or longer no more than twice per week (self-report).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use validated neuropsychological batteries cross-validated by supplementary measures (NIH Toolbox); operationalize social isolation with clear cutoffs (LSNS-6 ≤12) or behavioral thresholds; capture multi-modal outcomes including imaging and speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention effects evaluation plan (dose-specific and combined analyses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze the high dose (baseline to 6 months) and the maintenance dose (6 to 12 months) separately. Data will be analyzed to evaluate differences in cognitive function change and extent of social isolation from baseline to 6 months between intervention and control groups; similar analyses for 6 to 12 months; finally evaluate combined effects of high + maintenance dose on cognition and social isolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify contrasts for dose periods and combined effects; perform longitudinal comparisons between randomized groups at each interval and combined timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-design & staged intervention development (six steps for quality intervention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Previous research summarized six steps in developing a quality intervention: 1) defining and analyzing the problem; 2) identifying modifiable factors; 3) deciding on the intervention mechanism; 4) clarifying the intervention delivery process; 5) testing and revising the intervention; 6) conducting a more rigorous effectiveness evaluation. The proposed dissertation will address steps 1 to 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow a staged approach from problem analysis to delivery design before pilot testing and rigorous evaluation; use quantitative and qualitative data to identify modifiable targets and delivery preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor/co-sponsor selection and mentorship criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors selected for extensive domain expertise (gerontology, neurology, engineering, mixed-methods), mentorship records, and complementary skills. Sponsors contribute through weekly/regular meetings, methodological and content guidance (longitudinal analysis, qualitative/quantitative integration, clinical trial design, intervention development), and access to institutional resources and cores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select sponsors with relevant methodological and topical expertise, documented mentoring success, and institutional resources aligned with training goals; document planned frequency and modes of mentorship (weekly, monthly, journal clubs, investigator meetings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) — venues, topics, and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: RCR instruction is provided via: (a) research methods courses (small in-person groups, topics include ethical research conduct, conflict of interest, protecting human subjects, community-based research, peer review, publication ethics and authorship, responsibilities to humanity, avoiding and handling misconduct, ethical and unethical study designs; tenure-track faculty instruct; weekly 3–4 hour sessions for a semester); (b) professional development workshops and scholarly lectures (face-to-face discussion, 1–2 hours monthly, mandatory for doctoral students; topics include publishing ethics, authorship, peer review, study design, grant proposals, managing teams); (c) Hamovitch Center workshops/consultation; (d) IRB online courses (Human Subjects; Good Clinical Practice; Conflicts of Interest; HIPAA Privacy) with periodic refreshers; (e) CTSI Digital Scholar Training Program webinars on digital research practices (monthly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide layered RCR training across coursework, workshops, center consultations, and mandatory online IRB trainings; ensure refresher courses and participation in digital research practice webinars as needed.
